per_obligation_findings.notes: 8.1 'any user/cache-writable location' is implemented as the legacy dev-cache rejection + containment, not a writability probe — the correct reading (a probe would reject legitimate pip --user installs).

findings: Admission is replaced (manifest gate here vs legacy build_stamp + packaged-.ispc hashing in prepare — prepare_native_handle:283-302 is correctly forbidden on the default path by BUILD_DESIGN 8.2), lifetime is reused wholesale: native_handle._load_entries (eager argtypes/restype binding, native_handle.py:532-547), the NativeHandle class (pid pinning, execute, no dlclose), native_handle._dir_lock (installed_loader.py:616), the shared workflow-generation clock (:516-517), taxonomy re-export (:130-132).

PID pinning preserved: handle._pid captured from native_handle._getpid() at instantiate (:499) and re-resolved at call time by execute(); reviewer's REAL os.fork probe: parent handle raises StaleNativeHandle in the child, the child's auto_load mints a fresh CDLL under its own pid (keys embed pid) with bitwise-identical output, the parent handle keeps executing.

Workflow-generation bump semantics preserved: all loader caches key on wgen; new_workflow_generation clears native_handle._NEG_CACHE and makes installed-loader keys unreachable (tests :355-371, :450-460, :562-580). Minor cosmetic: _instantiate re-reads current_workflow_generation() rather than the wgen captured at entry — a mid-attempt bump by another thread only duplicates a handle, never reuses a stale one.

Dir-lock ordering: gate/hashing outside the lock, then lock -> recheck BOTH caches (:618 — strictly better than prepare's in-lock recheck, which skipped _NEG_CACHE; prior N8-10 note N3) -> instantiate -> publish inside the lock (:634-635). No in-process writer to the installed tree exists (auto never writes; expert_build is dev-cache-scoped and never entered), so outside-lock gating cannot observe half-published state.

TOCTOU verify->dlopen: the window exists (:590 verify vs :480 dlopen) but is EQUAL IN KIND to prepare_native_handle's (native_handle.py:580-583 hashes then CDLLs under a process-local lock no external writer honors). Trust root is the package manager (ARCHITECTURE.md: 'SHA checks provide content integrity, not authenticity'). No weakening. The additional _verified_manifest re-read (:639-643) adds a mid-load manifest re-parse whose non-taxonomy failures (KeyError/OSError) escape uncaught — only reachable via concurrent external mutation of the package tree mid-load; folded into note N1's broad-catch repair.

Registry publication difference is diagnostics-only: installed outcomes live in installed_loader._REGISTRY; nothing consults native_handle._REGISTRY for the installed tree, and the two cache systems cannot shadow each other (disjoint key spaces).

(a) content hash unverified: not achievable short of an external mid-load swap — the dlopen target is exactly the manifest-listed, hash-verified path (gate :455-459 + verify_generation build_native.py:607-613); nothing unlisted is ever opened.

(b) containment escape: lexical rejection of absolute/..//NUL/backslash-root components (:264-269) + realpath containment at member/generation/native-root/package-root levels; a symlinked member to a co-generation target hashes and dlopens the SAME bytes; the dev cache is rejected even for a fully valid generation (:557-562).

(c) ISA lying: unrecognized requirement strings fail closed (:348-350, test :757-765); the arm64/machine/minOS domain gates are loader-side constants, so an empty or lying requirements list cannot escape the qualified domain (reviewer probe: empty requirements loads on arm64 — within domain; N3 suggests positively requiring the expected cpu-feature strings).

(d) corrupt sibling poisoning: every candidate is gated (:577-597); a corrupt sibling is recorded (diagnostic key=None) while the qualified generation loads (reviewer probe + test :773-789); a crafted sibling cannot suppress the qualified one (declines append-and-continue).

Mutation teeth, 3 adversarial picks: (i) truncated-dylib-fixed-manifest — hash/name made consistent so only the Mach-O walk (or the dlopen failure, with a DIFFERENT message) can catch it; deleting macho_structure_error fails the keyword assertion — real teeth. (ii) math-profile-fast — validate_manifest accepts any non-empty id, so QUALIFIED_MATH_PROFILES (:439-446) is the ONLY defense; deleting it executes a fast-math dylib and the test fails — real teeth, loader-unique. (iii) abi-version-mismatch — SHARED teeth: validate_manifest independently rejects abi_version!=1 with a message containing the keyword, so deleting only the loader's gate would still pass the test; acceptable today because the loader's expectations ARE the imported builder constants (declared single-source-of-truth), noted as N4. Containment mutations additionally assert not-in-read_opens/not-hashed, proving rejection happened BEFORE any open — deleting _member_escape_reason would load the escaped file and fail the None expectation.

Merits: the sha256 manifest pin already fails any post-publication mutation (and mutated images cannot even load per the probe above); the scan's unique value — catching .s-re-emission vs linked-image divergence — is a build-machine property fixed at publication, needed exactly once where tools are guaranteed (build_native verify / N8-41); a runtime scan would violate 8.2's no-subprocess-at-load line and, /usr/bin/otool being an xcrun shim, convert clean-CLT hosts (ordinary supported state) into declines.
